title: Service definitions — shared across the vta/services/* spec family
description: A *service* is a transport the agent advertises in its own DID document: DIDComm mediation, a REST endpoint, TSP mediation, or a WebAuthn origin. Enabling or disabling one edits `service` in the agent's did:webvh document and republishes the signed log, so every mutation in this family produces a new log entry rather than flipping a runtime flag — which is why they all return `ServiceMutationResult`. These shapes are defined once because `enable`, `disable`, `update` and `rollback` return the same result, and `list` and `get` return the same state; an inline copy per task would fork the moment one of them gained a member.

ServiceKind.title: ServiceKind
ServiceKind.description: Which transport a task is acting on. This is the discriminator: it selects which member of `config` is meaningful, and a payload naming one kind with another's config is malformed rather than merely ignored.

ServiceState.title: ServiceState
ServiceState.description: What the agent currently advertises for one service. `enabled` is the only member every kind carries; the rest are kind-specific and absent when they do not apply. Note that `enabled: false` and an absent entry are different: the first says the agent knows about this transport and is not advertising it, the second says it has never been configured.

enabled.description: Whether the agent currently advertises this transport in its DID document.

mediatorDid.description: The mediator this transport routes through. Present for `didcomm` and `tsp`.

url.description: The advertised endpoint. Present for `rest` and `webauthn`.

drainsUntil.description: RFC 3339 instant at which a scheduled drain completes. Present only while a `didcomm` mediator is draining — see `vta/services/drain/list`.

ServiceMutationResult.title: ServiceMutationResult
ServiceMutationResult.description: The outcome of a change to an advertised service. Every member describes the **log entry the change produced**, because that is what the change actually is: the agent's DID document is the record, and a consumer that treats the response as a mere acknowledgement will miss that a redeploy may be required.

logEntryVersionId.description: Version id of the new did:webvh log entry this change wrote. Joins the change to the document's history.

effectiveAt.description: RFC 3339 instant the change took effect — the same instant stamped on the new log entry.

drainUntil.description: Present when the change scheduled a DIDComm drain. Its absence means no drain was scheduled, NOT that a drain finished instantly: a consumer reporting 'done' on an absent value would be right, and one reporting it on a present value would be wrong.

drainingMediator.description: The mediator being drained, when `drainUntil` is present.

vtaDid.description: The agent's own DID — subject of the log entry this change wrote. Carried so a caller can follow up without a second round trip.

serverless.description: True when the agent's DID is self-hosted. **The change is persisted locally but NOT published**: the operator must fetch the updated `did.jsonl` and redeploy before any verifier sees it. A consumer that ignores this reports success for a change no one else can observe yet.

DrainEntry.title: DrainEntry
DrainEntry.description: A DIDComm mediator that is no longer advertised but is still accepting delivery, so in-flight messages routed through it are not stranded.

endpoint.description: Where it is still reachable for the remainder of the drain.

drainsUntil.description: RFC 3339 instant after which the mediator is dropped and messages routed through it are lost.

RollbackResult.title: RollbackResult
RollbackResult.description: The outcome of a rollback. Distinct from ServiceMutationResult because a rollback can legitimately publish nothing: if the previous state already equals the current one there is no change to write, and `kind: "noOp"` says so with `logEntryVersionId` absent. Treating that as a failure would be wrong — the requested state holds — and treating it as an ordinary success would report a log entry that does not exist.

kind.description: What the rollback did. `disabled` re-disabled the transport, `enabled` re-advertised it at its prior settings, `updated` restored prior settings on an entry that stayed advertised, and `noOp` means the previous state already matched — nothing was written.

logEntryVersionId.description: Version id of the log entry the rollback wrote. **Absent when `kind` is `noOp`**, and present otherwise.

effectiveAt.description: RFC 3339 instant the rollback took effect. Absent for `noOp`.

drainingMediator.description: Present when rolling back DIDComm left a mediator draining.

serverless.description: True when the entry was written locally but not published — the operator must redeploy before any verifier sees it.
